client-generate.description: Generate a project's client from its provider's committed contract: a client project that names its provider in generatedFrom generates itself, and a provider that commits clientgen.json generates its in-module Go client.

clientgen-check.description: Fail on a tracked generated client, an invalid provider contract or inventory, or a handwritten first-party transport.

validate.description: Reject a tracked generated client and a new handwritten first-party transport for the whole workspace, once per session. It plans no generation: the guard reads committed inputs only.

client-generate-go.description: Generate the Go client of a project that names its provider in generatedFrom, from the provider's committed contract, into client.gen.go at the project root.

client.description: The generated Go client, the only file the emitter writes. It is built, not committed, so no drift policy judges it. The provider's contract reaches the key through the project's identity, which folds the contract's digest and the generation options. A contract with no first-party operation generates nothing. The projects that depend on the client project compile it, so the planner orders their jobs after this task (protocols/extension ADR 0014).

client-generate-ts.description: Generate the TypeScript client of a project that names its provider in generatedFrom, from the provider's committed contract, into the project's src tree.

client.description: The generated TypeScript sources, the only tree the emitter writes. The engine empties it before the task runs, so it holds what the last generation wrote and nothing else. It is built, not committed, so no drift policy judges it. The provider's contract reaches the key through the project's identity, which folds the contract's digest and the generation options. The projects that depend on the client project compile it, so the planner orders their jobs after this task (protocols/extension ADR 0014).

client-generate-module.description: Generate the in-module Go client a provider commits in clientgen.json, from the provider's own committed contract, and report the file it wrote.

moduleClientOutput.description: Project-relative path of the generated client.gen.go, inside the directory clientgen.json names in go.output.

client.description: The generated in-module Go client, the only file the emitter writes, at the go.output directory of clientgen.json inside the provider. It is built, not committed, so no drift policy judges it. A contract with no first-party operation generates nothing. The projects that depend on the provider compile it, so the planner orders their jobs after this task (protocols/extension ADR 0014).

clientgen-workspace-check.description: Validate provider discovery and the two inventories, report a generated client file in the Git candidate cut as clientgen.committed-generated-client, and scan all consumer sources for handwritten first-party transports, naming the generated binding to call. It builds nothing, generates nothing and spawns no Putnami. It reads the workspace's Git candidate cut (the tracked files and the untracked files no ignore rule excludes) and the member projects the job context names, which the CLI resolves from the committed workspace and scope manifests, and its key is the input `git:**`, which holds that cut. A file Git ignores is neither read nor keyed: the project index .putnami/workspace-index.json, a build's .gen output, every generated client and an ignored source are absent, as they are from a clone, so a provider's contract is its committed sidecar schema/openapi.json, its in-module client is the one its committed clientgen.json declares, and its other clients are the member projects whose committed putnami.json names its service in generatedFrom. A Git candidate under a project's .gen/clientgen or .gen/schema, a committed file or a build's output that no ignore rule excludes, is not a contract: the check reports it as clientgen.committed-generated-contract with the git command that takes it out. Editing, adding, deleting or renaming a candidate moves the key, so a cached verdict is replayed only for the bytes it judged, and the verdict is the same on a cold clone and on a tree the session just built.
